relations: Absolute pump-effort/error threshold constants do not transfer between plants: a supervisor tuned on a different tank system (different units, actuator range, and settling time) performed worse than no supervision at all when transplanted here unmodified (349 false positives, IAE 163 vs 95 for PID-only) because its thresholds were calibrated for that plant's scale, not this one's. Thresholds must be derived relative to this plant's own observed statistics (e.g. a ratio of recent-to-baseline effort within the telemetry window, or relative to nominal_target), not copied as fixed numbers.

This plant's default configuration (gamma_1=gamma_2=0.2) is in the non-minimum-phase regime, where most pump flow is routed through the delayed cross-coupling path rather than directly to its own tank. This causes real, sustained effort/error oscillation from control-loop interaction even with zero fault present - a naive 'any elevated effort is anomalous' rule will false-positive constantly on this normal background oscillation.

Comparing the first half of a telemetry window against its second half can only detect faults that ONSET inside the window: if the fault is already active when the window begins, the baseline half is contaminated and the diagnostic ratio stays near 1.0, so a persistent fault is systematically invisible no matter how large the threshold is set; a reference external to the window (nominal target or a sibling branch) is required.

In a plant with two symmetric branches, the ratio of effort-per-unit-sqrt(head) between the branches is itself a fault localizer: the healthy twin acts as a live reference, so a single-branch fault (leak) is detected even when it never clears and both branches are faulted from the start lose that asymmetry and need a second, per-tank signal.

A leak raises the effort needed to hold a head, so the effort/head ratio rises on the leaking branch; the cross-coupled twin often shows the OPPOSITE sign (extra cross-flow raises its level so its own pump backs off), meaning a detector that only flags ELEVATED effort/error naturally avoids false-positiving the coupled-but-healthy tank.

The signed-to-absolute error ratio (|mean error| / mean|error|) is a scale-free persistence indicator: a healthy non-minimum-phase loop oscillates around its setpoint (ratio low) while a fault that the loop cannot fully reject drives a one-sided error bias, so this ratio separates real faults from normal background oscillation without any absolute, plant-specific constant.

Normalising the cross-branch specific-effort ratio (pump effort per unit sqrt(head)) by its own early-window value cancels the plant's constant structural asymmetry (per-branch setpoint and hydraulic gain differences), so a twin-comparison detector stays silent in the healthy episode while still amplifying a single-branch fault whose onset lies inside the window.

A single scale-free error signal (level deficit relative to the nominal target, or signed-to-absolute error bias) is not sufficient on a non-minimum-phase plant: normal cross-coupled oscillation can push either one across threshold on its own, so anomaly flags must be the CONJUNCTION of an independent effort-based signal and an error-based signal, which keeps false positives at zero in never-faulted episodes.

When the supervisory setpoint reference and the diagnostic reference are the same nominal target, any setpoint reduction the supervisor itself makes is re-observed as a level deficit and can re-trigger the detector, creating a self-sustaining lower/restore loop; the reduction therefore has to be bounded well below the deficit threshold (here <= 2.5 cm, i.e. below ~8% of nominal).

For a leak on this plant the compensating effort rise is only ~1.2-1.4x because the non-minimum-phase coupling routes most flow through the delayed cross path, so any effort-ratio gate above ~1.3 is already blind to the fault regardless of how long the window is.

On this plant the closed loop fully absorbs a small leak in the tracking-error channel (episode IAE is bit-identical with and without any fault, 94.698 everywhere), so any detector whose primary evidence is error magnitude or error bias is structurally blind to it; the only persistent fault signature is the pump-effort-versus-head imbalance.

Because a leak raises the required effort and (if the loop saturates) lowers the head, the specific-effort ratio v/sqrt(h) has both effects pushing the SAME way, so the twin-branch asymmetry is amplified and never self-cancels - unlike a residual formed from the mass balance, whose sign flips depending on whether the controller compensates with effort or lets the level sag.

The healthy cross-branch specific-effort ratio is fixed by plant geometry and the nominal operating point (for gamma=0.2 it equals (0.8*u2/u1-0.2)/(0.8*u1/u2-0.2) with u_i=sqrt(h_i)), so a model-implied nominal offset sym0 lets a twin-comparison detector work even when the two tank setpoints are different, whereas assuming sym0=0 would false-positive under unequal setpoints.

Requiring the whole-window and the recent-half statistics to give the same directional verdict separately rejects random oscillation-driven false positives (limit-cycle swings average out over a full period but not consistently across two nested windows) while still firing on a genuinely persistent fault, giving persistence filtering without needing any absolute threshold.

In the cross-dominant four-tank (gamma=0.2) a leak on tank 1 is compensated mainly by pump 2, which feeds tank 1 through tank 3 with weight (1-gamma)=0.8, while pump 1 (direct weight 0.2) actually backs off: solving the steady-state balances gives v2-v1 = q1/((1-2*gamma)*k), so the specific-effort ratio (v1/sqrt(h1))/(v2/sqrt(h2)) FALLS for a tank-1 leak and RISES for a tank-2 leak - the opposite sign to the naive 'the leaking branch's own effort rises' heuristic, so a twin-ratio detector must map a LOW ratio to tank 1.

Because the leak is fully rejected by the loop (levels track, episode IAE is fault-invariant), the only observable is the pump-effort-versus-head imbalance; comparing the twin branches' specific effort v/sqrt(h) against the plant-geometry reference works with faults present from the very first sample, whereas any baseline drawn from the window itself stays contaminated and blind.

A twin-branch specific-effort ratio is structurally blind to a symmetric double leak (equal faults on both branches) because the ratio stays exactly at its healthy value; reducing missed detections in both_leaks requires a separate absolute (model-gain) reference, not a sharper ratio threshold.

A gate whose threshold lies outside the physical dynamic range of its own statistic is not a conservative detector but a silent no-op: an ELEVATED_RATIO gate of 1.8 applied to a plant whose fault-driven effort change is only ~1.2-1.4x never fires on ANY scenario, so the supervisor still returns a per-tank diagnosis while its whole score collapses to IAE + 300 x (fault-active steps). The first check on any detector should be that its statistic actually crosses its threshold on at least one faulty scenario.

In this scoring budget a step of detection latency on a genuine fault costs 300, a step of false positive on a tank that never faults costs 800, and a false positive in the never-faulted baseline episode is fatal (promotion tolerance ~0); the detector must therefore be tuned to guarantee literally zero flags on the never-faulted branch and only then made as fast as possible - a threshold chosen to balance FP and FN rates is systematically suboptimal here.

Because the outer loop nulls the level error completely (episode IAE is bit-identical with and without any fault, 94.698), the missed-anomaly count of a supervisor is a pure measure of detector silence/latency, not of threshold accuracy - so miss counts can be used directly as a latency budget when tuning a detector on this plant, and any detector whose primary evidence is error magnitude or error bias has exactly the same score as no detector at all.

With a silent detector the per-scenario score is just 94.698 + 300 x fault-active-steps, so the milder but longer episodes (250-step leaks) score WORSE than the more severe but shorter ones (199 steps): scenario ranking under a blind supervisor reflects fault DURATION, not fault severity, so tuning against the visible ranking can mislead.

The tracking-error channel of this plant is completely fault-invariant (episode IAE is bit-identical at 94.698 across every scenario, faulted or not), so a supervisory setpoint change cannot improve the IAE term at all - the setpoint channel is score-neutral and only the detection-latency term and the false-positive term move the score; the optimum is a pure detector plus a restoration policy that never leaves a residual gap.

Because the twin specific-effort reference is evaluated from the measured heads (u=sqrt(h)) rather than the commanded setpoints, a supervisor that lowers the flagged branch's demand enlarges that branch's relative leak and pushes the diagnostic deviation further from 1.0, so a bounded demand reduction cannot mask its own fault trigger or re-trigger the detector - the self-sustaining lower/restore loop only appears when the diagnostic and the setpoint reference are the same signal.

A zero false-positive result on the never-faulted baseline is not evidence that a detector works: a supervisor whose gates are individually unreachable (here an effort-ratio gate of 1.8 against a plant whose fault-driven effort change is ~1.2-1.4x, AND-ed with an error gate of 0.03 against a loop whose error channel is bit-identically fault-invariant) is identically silent, and silence scores exactly like a perfectly tuned detector on the baseline. Only the faulted scenarios' missed-anomaly counts separate a working detector from a no-op, so a conjunction of two signals must have each term checked for individual reachability on faulty data before it is trusted as a persistence filter.

The 'separate absolute model-gain reference' proposed for a symmetric double leak cannot actually be built from the telemetry window: at steady state there are two measured mass-balance equations and three unknowns (common plant gain, q1, q2), so an equal leak on both branches leaves no signature at all - it is unobservable unless the fault onset (a transient) lies inside the window. A candidate whose only diagnostic is a twin ratio therefore has a hard score floor of roughly (94.7 + 300*400)/6 ~ 2.0e4 on this battery, because the 120094-point both_leaks scenario survives untouched.

False-positive cost is not uniform within one episode: on any branch whose own fault never activates a flag costs 800, while on a branch that is itself faulted it costs only 160, so the correct design bias is a statistic that is automatically anti-correlated with the healthy twin's demand rather than a symmetric magnitude threshold. The cross-branch effort/head ratio has this property for free - the leaking branch's own pump throttles back while its cross-coupled partner takes the load - so the twin-ratio detector's residual FP risk lives almost entirely in the never-faulted baseline and in the settling window right after a fault clears, not in faulted episodes.

The measured fault-free episode supplies an absolute external anchor for this plant - total pump effort v1+v2 sits at 17.77 V and the cross-branch split v1-v2 at 3.05 V - and a leak on EITHER branch raises the total in proportion to the total leak while only the SIGN of the split encodes the faulted branch; gating the split-based localiser with a total-effort excess makes a detector robust to whichever oscillation mode dominates, because the anti-phase healthy mode moves the split while leaving the total alone and the in-phase mode moves the total while leaving the split alone, so neither pure mode can satisfy both conditions at once.

This plant's healthy instantaneous effort ranges (v1 1.92-12 V, v2 2.58-12 V) are wider than any plausible leak signature (1.2-1.4x on one pump), so no instantaneous or single-sample statistic can separate fault from no-fault; usable thresholds must be expressed in units of the standard error of a window aggregate, i.e. scale as sqrt(SD1^2+SD2^2)/sqrt(n_eff) with n_eff discounted well below n for the slow cross-coupled oscillation, rather than as fixed volts or fixed ratios.

The two branches are not interchangeable: pump 1's healthy mean (10.41 V) sits only 1.59 V below the 12 V rail while pump 2's (7.36 V) sits 4.64 V below it, so a fault whose compensation must flow through the near-rail pump has its effort signature clipped and is intrinsically much harder to detect than the mirrored fault; detector thresholds must be branch-asymmetric (or rail-aware) rather than a single symmetric band.

When the false-positive penalty (160-250 per step) is below the missed-anomaly penalty (300 per step), a leak-presence gate combined with an imperfect branch localiser still has positive expected value even when the localiser occasionally attributes the fault to the wrong tank, whereas an ungated per-branch deviation statistic is catastrophic because it fires on the ordinary anti-phase load swings that are present with no fault at all.

On a plant whose error channel is fault-invariant, commanding nominal setpoints unconditionally is strictly optimal rather than merely safe: it makes the restore-gap term identically zero and keeps the supervisor's own demand change out of the only usable diagnostic, so every effort signature in the window is attributable to the plant and not to the supervisor's past actions.

The episode-start fill transient impersonates a severe fault in the effort channel: both controllers drive their pumps to the 12 V rail (v1+v2 approaching the 24 V ceiling against a 17.77 V healthy mean) while the split collapses toward 0 (against a 3.05 V healthy mean), so the total-effort and split statistics are simultaneously fault-like; the only usable discriminator is the |error| channel (block mean ~0.25 m during filling versus 0.074 m healthy, max 0.19 m), and it is usable as a guard precisely because it is fault-invariant, i.e. it can never suppress a genuine detection that the unfaulted episode would have allowed.

The leak signature has an invariant SHAPE, not just an invariant sign: solving the two steady-state branch balances when the loop fully rejects the fault gives delta(v1+v2) = q and delta(v1-v2) = -q/(1-2*gamma) for a tank-1 leak (mirror-signed for tank 2), so the split always moves 1/(1-2*gamma) = 1.667x as much as the total, independently of leak size; a detector that requires a simultaneous total excess AND a split displacement of the OPPOSITE sign with magnitude between roughly 0.5x and 5x the total excess is therefore a shape test that stays valid for any fault magnitude yet rejects both pure oscillation modes.

A detector may safely pair an EXTERNAL location anchor (the measured healthy means 17.77 V total and 3.05 V split, which the telemetry window cannot contaminate) with an INTERNAL scale anchor (the current window's own standard deviation, which a leak barely changes because it shifts the effort distribution rather than widening it); this hybrid survives both the fill transient and the oscillation phase, whereas a fully self-referential baseline is blinded by contamination and a fully fixed absolute threshold is either unreachable or false-positive-prone at this plant's scale.

The error guard has selective power that a pure silence/persistence filter does not: every healthy false-positive mode that raises effort on BOTH branches at once (episode-start double saturation) necessarily requires both levels to sit far below their targets, i.e. a block-mean |error| of ~0.25 m versus 0.074-0.083 m healthy, whereas a genuine symmetric double leak raises both branch efforts with the error channel untouched; gating on block-mean |error| > 0.115 therefore removes the symmetric false-positive class while preserving the symmetric true-positive class (both_leaks), which is otherwise unreachable by any split-ratio test.

Episode length is recoverable from the published numbers themselves: combined IAE 94.698 divided by the healthy per-step combined |error| (0.0740 + 0.0832) gives ~600 steps, while fault-active windows are only 199-250 steps, i.e. under half the episode; a detector can therefore afford an 80-sample averaging window and still leave more than half of every fault's active steps detectable, so the binding constraint on detection latency is the fault's duty cycle rather than the supervisor's reaction time.

When the analysis window is long relative to the fault's rise, requiring the recent half of that window to reproduce the whole-window verdict is almost free in latency: at every step after fault onset the half-window contains a strictly larger faulted fraction than the full window, so the half condition is satisfied no later than the full condition; the persistence filter therefore buys reduced spurious-exceedance probability rather than costing missed steps, and only bites when the analysis window is short compared with the fault duration.

The both-rails saturation state that counterfeits a leak is eliminated by the shape band alone, independent of the error guard: at v1 = v2 = 12 V (the extreme of the measured healthy pump ranges) the total sits at 24 V (dt = +6.23 V) but the split collapses to 0 (ds = -3.05 V), so |ds|/dt = 0.49 falls below the 0.6 lower edge of the 1.667-centred band, meaning the measured healthy extremes of both pumps cannot jointly satisfy the total-excess and shape conditions in any oscillation phase.

Because the healthy per-pump standard deviations are known (2.27 V and 3.16 V), the worst-case standard error of the window-mean total effort is bounded by sqrt(2.27^2 + 3.16^2)/sqrt(n_eff) = 3.89/sqrt(n_eff) regardless of the unknown cross-correlation, so with a 10-effective-sample window no correlation structure can force a threshold above 2.2 x 3.89/sqrt(10) ~ 2.7 V; leaks whose equivalent pump-voltage magnitude q (which enters as delta(v1+v2) = q and delta(v1-v2) = -q/(1-2*gamma)) exceeds ~2.7 V are detectable by the total-excess statistic on any correlation structure, which fixes a hard detectability floor for this battery.

Because a leak shifts the effort distribution rather than widening it, the window's own per-sample total-effort standard deviation stays essentially at its healthy value even when a fault is present, so using that in-window deviation only to scale the threshold (rather than as a baseline mean) is self-calibrating without suffering the contamination blindness that kills mean-vs-own-mean residual detectors.

The shape band alone does NOT exclude the episode-start fill transient; only the joint-rail extreme does. At v1=v2=12 the split collapses to 0 and |ds|/dt = 3.05/6.23 = 0.49, which falls below the 0.6 lower edge and is rejected by shape, but the intermediate fill state v1=v2~10 V gives dt=2.23 and ds=-3.05, i.e. |ds|/dt = 1.37, which sits squarely INSIDE the leak band and would false-flag a tank-1 leak; the fill must therefore be excluded by the error guard (block-mean |error| ~0.25 m during filling vs 0.074-0.083 m healthy), not by the shape test.

Because the two cross-coupled pumps move dominantly anti-phase (v1 up <=> v2 down), the split v1-v2 is the high-variance channel (its healthy swings are comparable to its own 3.05 V mean) while the total v1+v2 is the quiet channel (anti-phase cancellation keeps its standard deviation well below the naive sqrt(SD1^2+SD2^2)=3.89 V); accordingly the total must carry the magnitude/threshold test and the split only the direction/shape test, because any per-pump or split-magnitude threshold must be raised above the individual pumps' own 2.27-3.16 V standard deviations and thereby becomes unreachable for the ~1.2-1.4x fault signature.

Choosing a trailing block length B sets detection latency to roughly B*DT_THR/q steps into a fault (the block mean only reaches (k/B)*q after k faulted samples), so on this 600-step plant with 199-250-step faults the window is a latency/FP dial: B=100 with DT_THR=2.5 V costs ~60-90 missed steps of a real fault but keeps the 100-sample total-effort mean within ~2 standard errors of the healthy anchor, whereas shortening B to react faster trades a linear latency gain for a 1/sqrt(B) loss in baseline FP margin on the one scenario where any FP is fatal.

A 'split not displaced' test must be absolute, not a ratio: the balanced double leak leaves the split sitting on its healthy anchor (ds ~ 0 V against SPLIT_ANCHOR=3.05), whereas the episode-start fill collapses the split toward zero (ds = -3.05 V) while raising the total; both states give a SMALL |ds|/dt once the total is large, so any ratio-based 'split unchanged' criterion is satisfied by both and needs the error guard, while requiring |split_mean - 3.05| < 1.2 V separates them with no help from any other channel.

A split-sign localiser has an intrinsic blind spot for unbalanced double faults: for simultaneous leaks q1, q2 the total excess is q1+q2 and the split displacement is 1.667*(q2-q1), so whenever |q2-q1| > 0.7*(q1+q2)/1.667 the both_leaks episode falls into the single-branch (directional) band and only ONE tank is ever flagged, leaving the other tank's full fault window as missed-anomaly cost; only a near-balanced leak (|q2-q1| small relative to q1+q2) can reach the symmetric branch, so both branches must be evaluated on every step and OR-ed rather than treated as a mutually exclusive classification.

On this plant the usable design window for the total-effort threshold is only about 3.7 V wide: the physical ceiling is 24 V (both pumps at their measured 12 V maxima) while the block-mean noise floor sits at 17.77 + ~2.5 V, so any total-excess threshold must live in (20.3, 24) V; the lower edge is set by the anti-phase coupling that keeps the total quiet, and raising the threshold toward the rail buys false-positive margin only by giving up the entire sub-3 V fault class, which is why FP-safety and detectability are simultaneously marginal here rather than independently tunable.

The champion's whole 64.9k deficit is missed_anomaly cost with exactly zero false positives, and the baseline false-positive tolerance is effectively zero while faulted scenarios keep a ~15%/100-point allowance, so the admissibility test for a new detector runs the opposite way round from the usual one: every gate must be individually UNREACHABLE by the measured healthy envelope (block-mean total <= 20.3 V, block-mean |error| <= 0.085 m) before it is worth adding, because a joint gate set that the healthy data can only breach with all-and'd conditions is still fatal on the one scenario where any single flag costs the whole candidate.

The two flag paths needed to cover single-branch and balanced-double leaks are mutually exclusive by construction as long as the leak shape is trusted: a single-branch leak produces |split deviation| = 1.667 x total excess, which exceeds any 'split undisplaced' tolerance (<= 1.0 V) the moment the total excess clears a >= 3 V magnitude gate, so an undirected branch can only add flags in episodes where no single branch dominates - this bounds the cost of adding it to the false-positive risk of the never-faulted baseline and of the near-balanced double-leak episode alone, and makes the undirected bar the only free parameter that trades both_leaks coverage against baseline safety.

A guard derived from the fault-invariant error channel is strictly cheaper than the equivalent tightening of the magnitude threshold: because a genuine fault leaves block-mean |error| at the healthy 0.074-0.083 m level, raising the error-guard bar can only ever exclude the start-up fill state (~0.25 m) and can never exclude a real detection, whereas every extra volt added to the total-excess threshold permanently deletes an entire band of leak magnitudes from detectability - so the budget for false-positive safety should be spent on guards first and on threshold height only afterwards.

The 12 V per-pump rail caps the leak signature asymmetrically and hard: solving the compensated branch balances with delta(v1+v2)=q and delta(v1-v2)=-/+1.667q gives tank-1 v2=7.36+1.333q<=12 -> q<=3.48 V and tank-2 v1=10.41+1.333q<=12 -> q<=1.19 V, so the total-excess statistic has a physical ceiling of 3.48 V for tank-1 faults and 1.19 V for tank-2 faults against a healthy block-mean noise floor of about 2.5 V; the whole usable threshold window is under 1 V wide and any tank-2 total-excess detection is geometrically impossible.

For any block whose mean total exceeds about 20 V the per-pump rails force the block-mean split into [T-24, 24-T], so at a 3 V total excess the split may only sit within +/-3 V of zero mean; a large total excess can therefore only be carried by a NEGATIVE split displacement, i.e. every high-total excursion on this plant is directionally tank-1-like by rail geometry alone, and the mirrored tank-2 directional branch can never fire at any magnitude gate above ~1.2 V.

A split-anchored symmetric (balanced double leak) branch is self-defeating under the rails: requiring |mean(v1)-mean(v2)-3.05| < 1.2 V caps the block-mean total at 2*v1max - 1.85 = 22.15 V, so any symmetric-branch threshold above dT = 4.38 V is unreachable by healthy data but equally unreachable by a balanced double leak - the branch is either unsafe or vacuous, which is the geometric form of the both_leaks unobservability floor.

The episode-start fill couples the magnitude and the error conditions instead of decoupling them: reaching a block-mean total of 20.7 V from the healthy 17.77 V requires roughly 80 percent of the 100-sample block to be fill, which forces the same block's mean|error| to about 0.18 m against a 0.105 m guard, so the total-excess gate and the error guard cannot be satisfied on the same block - the false-positive class is excluded by construction rather than by tuning.

An error floor of 0.03 m in a mean|error| gate is inert, not conservative: the healthy steady-state mean|error| is 0.074-0.083 m, so such a term is true at every step and the whole decision is carried by the effort term it was meant to protect; any error-based guard on this plant must sit ABOVE 0.083 m to do any work and below about 0.13 m to preserve steady-state detectability.

For any fixed-length block-mean detector with a step-like disturbance of steady-state excursion Q and a threshold THR < Q, the onset latency and the post-clear false-flag tail are complements that always sum to exactly the block length B: the detector misses the first B*THR/Q steps of the disturbance and keeps firing for B*(1 - THR/Q) steps after it ends. The total 'contamination' of a fault episode is therefore fixed at B steps no matter how the threshold is tuned; the threshold only decides how that fixed B is split between missed steps and post-clear false steps, so with a missed-step cost (300) higher than a faulted-scenario false-step cost (160) the optimal split biases the threshold DOWN toward the healthy-envelope floor, not up toward the physical ceiling.

The episode-start symmetric fill traverses a straight line in (total, split) space from the healthy anchor (17.77, 3.05) toward (24, 0), so for any block whose mean total already clears a 3.0 V magnitude gate (T >= 20.77) the fill's shape ratio (split deviation)/(total excess) is at most 3.05/3.0 = 1.017 and falls to 0.49 at the rail. Consequently a shape band whose lower edge is set at 1.05-1.1 rejects the ENTIRE symmetric-fill family by geometry alone, independently of the error channel; the error guard is then a redundant second line of defence rather than the only thing standing between the fill and a false positive, which means the error guard's threshold can be shifted without opening a new false-positive path.

Because a leak's total excess and its split displacement are both first-order in the fault magnitude and both scale linearly with the faulted fraction of the block, the shape ratio is invariant not only for any leak size but also along the entire rise and fall of the fault, where the block is a mixture of healthy and faulted samples (both deviations are scaled by the same mixture factor). This makes the shape test safe to evaluate on a shorter nested confirmation sub-block at partial saturation, and means only the magnitude gate, not the shape band, carries the detectability-versus-false-positive trade-off.
